transcript: A bunch of the Odyssey cast members have Oscars or Oscar nominations, but can you guess which two of them have Tony Awards? Not Jon Bernthal. He did recently make his Broadway debut, and I actually think he probably should have been nominated, but unfortunately he did not. Not Tom Holland. He did play Billy Elliot when he was an adorable little kid, but he was not one of the three boys who originated the role on Broadway and shared the Tony Award. In fact while he's done a couple of stage shows in London, he's never been on Broadway. Similarly, Anne Hathaway has a short but intriguing history of performing on stage, but all of the shows she's done have been off Broadway, not on Broadway, so she's never been eligible for Tony. There are two actors from the Odyssey who have been *nominated* for the Tony but never won, including Lupita Nyong’o, who was in Eclipsed. and hot take: I think she should have won over Jessica Lange for Long Day's Journey tonight. The other Tony nominee in the Odyssey is Corey Hawkins, who was nominated twice, actually, for Six Degrees of separation and Top Dog Underdog. And honestly, I think he should have won for either or both of these. He's a phenomenal stage actor. But like I said, there are two actors from the Odyssey who *do* have Tony Awards, one of whom is John Leguizamo, who I think kind of got back on a lot of people's Radar with his role in the Odyssey, he gave a really good performance, but he's been doing stage work for years, most notably in his solo shows that he both writes and performs. And he actually got a special non-competitive Tony Award for his show Latin History for morons, which you can actually go watch on Netflix incidentally. The only actor from the Odyssey to win a competitive Tony Award is Bill Irwin for who's afraid of Virginia Wolf. And as you might know from some of the behind the scenes materials, Bill Irwin did play the Cyclops in the Odyssey with a composite of prosthetics and puppetry, of course, utilizing his long history of movement work in addition to traditional acting.
